clue.text: Part of oath of loyalty also suggests poor rationing

parts.note: also and and both add something further
a single portion to be shared by everybody is meagre rationing indeed

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a loyalty pledge sounds like a description of a stingy food allowance.
explanation.walkthrough: The second piece is read literally: one portion for the whole company is poor rationing. The full phrase is the Three Musketeers' motto, 'all for one and one for all'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Musketeers' pledge of mutual loyalty ends with this phrase, so it is one part of that oath.

clue.text: Capital buried in open air obituary

indicators.note: buried in says the answer lies concealed within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A capital city turns up tucked inside a newspaper death notice written outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Kenya's seat of government is this city, so it is a capital.

clue.text: Neglect love calling

parts.note: love is nil in tennis scoring, written as the letter O
a calling, a vocation, is one's mission in life

explanation.surface: Someone frets that neglect of a loved one comes from devotion to their vocation.
explanation.definitionFit: A failure to do something one should is an act of neglect, a synonym.

clue.text: Currency used by most of the continent

indicators.note: most of says the final part of the word is cut away, leaving the greater share

parts.note: the continent, to a Briton, is mainland Europe

explanation.surface: A remark that one currency is in use across most of the European mainland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most of' drops the last two letters, PE.
explanation.definitionFit: The money shared by much of the European Union is an example of a currency.

clue.text: Has too much ancestry concealed by deliveries

indicators.note: concealed by says one word is hidden inside the other, here the ancestry word within the deliveries word

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries, so deliveries suggests overs
one's stock is one's lineage or ancestry

explanation.surface: A family's lineage gets lost behind a pile of parcels that have been delivered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deliveries' points at the post, but here it is cricket: an over is a set of six balls bowled. 'Has too much' is the verb, as a shop overstocks.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop holding surplus goods keeps more inventory than it needs, which is excess.

clue.text: Makes no difference, adding right to roam

definitions.text: Makes no difference, adding right to roam

parts.words: Makes no difference, adding right to roam
parts.note: a word for wandering which keeps the same meaning when the letter for right is put in front of it

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs that granting a right to roam changes nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Put R (right) in front of AMBLE and you get RAMBLE, which also means to roam: adding right makes no difference to the meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: To stroll at leisure is to wander about, and so is a ramble, the same word with R in front.

clue.text: Quite big whip traps right soldier

indicators.note: traps says the whip word encloses the other letters, catching them inside

parts.note: a lash is a whip
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A rather big whip catches a soldier on the right.
explanation.definitionFit: Somewhat sizeable means on the large side, fairly but not hugely big.

clue.text: Computer to manufacture anagrams?

definitions.meaning: a machine or program for writing and editing documents
something that processes words, rearranging them as an anagram does

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a computer could churn out anagrams.
explanation.definitionFit: The software for typing documents is a computer application, and literally it is a thing that processes words, as anagram-making does.

clue.text: Labour is a prerequisite for her

definitions.text: Labour is a prerequisite for her

parts.words: Labour is a prerequisite for her
parts.note: labour read twice: paid work makes her employed, and labour in childbirth makes her a parent

explanation.surface: A remark that a certain woman must first be in labour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' is both employment and giving birth; a mother with a job needs both kinds.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman with children who also has paid employment is one who has given birth and has a job.

clue.text: Actor puts one in a twist

indicators.note: in says the one-letter piece is placed inside the other word

parts.note: Oliver Twist is the Dickens orphan, so a Twist could be Oliver
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: An actor manages to put one into a contortion.
explanation.walkthrough: Oliver Twist is the Dickens orphan; I goes in after OLIV.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence, the great English stage and screen performer, bore this surname.

clue.text: Grab me back, getting round ban

indicators.note: back says the words grab me are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a round object resembles the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone pleads to be grabbed back, finding a way round a prohibition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' turns GRABME into EMBARG; 'getting' just adds the O.
explanation.definitionFit: An official prohibition on trade with a country is a ban.

clue.text: Refuse bone-cutting doctors

indicators.note: cutting says the bone word slices into the doctors word, sitting inside it

parts.note: DR is short for doctor, so DRS is doctors
os is Latin for bone, used in anatomy

explanation.surface: Doctors decline to do any bone surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' is the noun, rubbish, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Worthless waste matter is rubbish, another word for refuse.

clue.text: Star kites are destroyed

indicators.note: destroyed says the letters are wrecked and rebuilt in another order

parts.note: the fodder words, which as printed carry an E where the anagram needs a second S

explanation.surface: Kites shaped like stars are wrecked.
explanation.walkthrough: As printed, KITES ARE has an E where the answer needs a second S: the setter's fodder is a letter off, and 'destroyed' rearranges the letters as intended.
explanation.definitionFit: The printed symbol shaped like a little star is this mark, so star describes it.

clue.text: Herbs smell badly inside swamp with headless insects

parts.note: a fen is marshy, swampy ground

indicators.note: inside says the smell word goes within the shortened insects word
headless says the first letter is removed

parts.note: bugs are insects
to reek is to stink, to smell badly

explanation.surface: Herbs growing in a marsh give off a foul smell among decapitated insects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smell badly' reads as a description of the herb, but it is the piece that goes in, after the insects word has lost its head. Fenugreek seeds are a curry spice.
explanation.definitionFit: Fenugreek is an aromatic plant used in cooking and medicine, an example of a herb.

clue.text: Animal horn costlier when decored and crushed

indicators.note: crushed says the letters are mashed up and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: decored says the core, the middle letters, are taken out of the word

explanation.surface: An animal's horn becomes dearer once cored and ground, as in a sad trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decored' takes the central TL out of COSTLIER, leaving COSIER; 'crushed' then rearranges HORN with COSIER.
explanation.definitionFit: The large thick-skinned African or Asian beast with a horned snout is an animal.

clue.text: Pruned object?

indicators.note: pruned says the word is cut back, losing its final letter

parts.note: a thing is an object

explanation.surface: A question about what an object becomes after pruning.
explanation.walkthrough: Cut the last letter off THING and you have what pruning does: it thins.
explanation.definitionFit: Pruning a plant reduces its branches, so a pruned object has been made sparser.

clue.text: Bid of one no trump captures street cops

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: captures says the first group of letters takes the second into its middle

parts.note: NT is the bridge abbreviation for no trumps
the RUC was the Royal Ulster Constabulary, the Northern Ireland police

explanation.surface: A bridge bid of one no trump is overtaken by police on the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bid' looks like bridge, matching the surface, but it is the verb: to bid is to order. The RUC was Northern Ireland's police force until 2001.
explanation.definitionFit: To bid someone do something is to tell or order them, a synonym.

clue.text: Frightens company with different directions

parts.note: W and S are two compass points, west and south

explanation.surface: A business scares people by heading every which way.
explanation.definitionFit: To intimidate someone into submission is to cow them, so frightens fits.

clue.text: Desiring to be inadequate

definitions.meaning: longing for or wishing to have something
lacking, falling short of what is needed

explanation.surface: Someone notes that craving something is a sign of being not good enough.
explanation.definitionFit: To want is to desire, and something found lacking is deficient or short.

clue.text: Actor prancing before the palace

parts.note: a horse bucking is leaping and prancing about
a ham is an overacting actor

explanation.surface: A showy actor capers about in front of the royal residence.
explanation.walkthrough: The parts come in reverse order to the clue: the prancing comes first. It is the monarch's London residence.
explanation.definitionFit: The London residence of the British sovereign is the best-known royal palace.

clue.text: Freight spoils with maturity

parts.note: a haul is a thief's take, the spoils
age is maturity, the condition of being old

explanation.surface: Cargo is ruined as it gets older.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoils' is the noun, booty, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The carrying of goods by road, or the goods carried, is cargo transport.

clue.text: Money for nothing is the function of medicine

parts.note: sine is a trigonometric function
a cure is a medicine or remedy

explanation.surface: Getting paid without working is presented as a doctor's remedy.
explanation.definitionFit: A post with pay but no real duties is a cushy job, effectively money for nothing.

clue.text: Feature a service

parts.note: the chin is a facial feature

explanation.surface: Something is presented as a feature of a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' is a set of crockery, a dinner or tea service.
explanation.definitionFit: A matching set of porcelain plates and cups is a dinner service.

clue.text: Bound by reported confidence

indicators.note: reported says the word is passed on by ear, a near-identical sound

parts.note: trussed means tied up, bound

explanation.surface: Someone is tied to a promise of discretion that was told to others.
explanation.definitionFit: Faith or reliance placed in someone is a synonym of confidence.

clue.text: Reflect type of location

definitions.meaning: to send back sound or repeat, as a canyon does
the bat's way of finding things by bounced sound, prefixed to location

explanation.surface: Someone ponders a sort of place.
explanation.definitionFit: To reflect sound is to resound, and echolocation is navigation by bounced sound.

clue.text: Alternative provided by diamond opening

parts.note: or introduces an alternative
if means provided that
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: An option is made available thanks to a diamond's opening.
explanation.definitionFit: A hole or aperture, especially in the body, is an opening.

clue.text: Struggle to use card shuffle

indicators.note: shuffle says the letters are mixed like a pack of cards before a deal

explanation.surface: A card player is told to shuffle the pack.
explanation.definitionFit: A vigorous campaign for a cause is a fight or struggle.

clue.text: Good girl loses nerve to hold wine in these, perhaps

parts.note: a lass is a girl
in British slang to bottle it is to lose one's nerve

explanation.surface: A well-behaved young woman chickens out of keeping wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottle it' is British slang for losing one's nerve.
explanation.definitionFit: Wine is commonly stored in containers made of glass, so these are examples of wine vessels.
